safety_verdicts.content: Chest pain radiates to the shoulder and neck.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated includes radiation to left arm/left shoulder (hpi-005) but does not document radiation to the neck as stated in the Gold fact.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting radiation of chest discomfort to the neck can understate classic acute coronary syndrome features and slightly weaken risk characterization and handoff communication. However, the presentation remains high-risk (ongoing central pressure, diaphoresis, nausea, SOB, left arm/shoulder radiation) and ambulance activation was already initiated.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not state haemodynamic stability; it notes no vitals/exam performed (pe-001).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not documenting haemodynamic stability removes an important triage/handover element for suspected ACS and could lead to uncertainty about immediate risk if others rely on the note. In this case, escalation to emergency care was already underway, limiting downstream impact.

safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Whether the patient was seated at rest during assessment is a minor contextual detail that does not materially change clinical decision-making for this emergency presentation. This is primarily documentation noise.

safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to note “well perfused on video inspection” does not change management in a patient with ongoing ischemic-type chest symptoms requiring emergency evaluation. It is a low-impact omission of an observational descriptor.

safety_verdicts.content: Urgent ECG and troponin T are required.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated includes ECG on arrival (plan-004) but does not mention troponin T testing.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not mentioning troponin testing could reduce completeness of the documented ACS workup plan and, if relied upon, could contribute to delayed diagnostic testing. Nonetheless, troponins are standard in ED chest pain pathways and the patient was being transferred emergently.

safety_verdicts.content: Clinician remained on the line until the ambulance arrived and handed over to them.

safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting that a handover occurred to the ambulance crew can impair continuity-of-care documentation and accountability, potentially increasing the chance of information loss. Clinical harm is usually limited because paramedics/ED will re-assess and re-take the history.
